stories.label: Iran threatens to 'rain down hell' if US escalates war
stories.summary: Araghchi's ultimatum answers Trump's 'locked and loaded' warning, on the day Trump meets Qatar's prime minister, Washington's channel to Tehran, at the White House, and after Trump claimed Iran would have signed a deal but for the midterms. Lead with the ultimatum and who carries the messages; note that Iranian state media report fresh US strikes on Qeshm Island, attributed as such, not stated as fact. The prediction market on the Israel-Iran ceasefire holding to 15 November has climbed from 65% to 89% this week.

stories.label: Iraq has agreed with the US to allow oil exports through Hormuz, minister says
stories.summary: Iraq, which sells nearly all its crude by sea, says the Iran war and the export disruption have cost it $60 billion, and it now has US understandings for a lane hugging Oman. Lead with the $60 billion and the dependence of Iraq's budget on one strait; add that an IRGC Navy official told Iranian state media navigation aids in the south of the strait were destroyed and no 'unauthorised' vessel transited overnight (Reuters), so who authorises passage is the open question. Series: Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Drone attack suspends production at Iraq's Khor Mor gasfield
stories.summary: Khor Mor feeds the power stations that supply roughly 2,800 megawatts to Iraqi Kurdistan, so a drone strike on one field turns into blackouts for millions of households. Lead with the electricity the field carries and who goes dark; note that the field has been hit repeatedly and no one has been held to account. Series: natural gas.

stories.label: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with US Congress looms
stories.summary: The first weekend after losing Congress: Trump promised to double down on the immigration crackdown while also conceding to CBS (Bloomberg) that deportations may have been 'too tough' and cost his party, and Hakeem Jeffries backed impeaching Defence Secretary Hegseth as Democrats plan committee probes (Al Jazeera). Lead with the contradiction between the concession and the doubling down; the mechanism is what a House majority can do — subpoenas, impeachment, appropriations — to an administration that refuses concessions.

stories.label: Zamfara Attack: Council chair says 12 family members killed
stories.summary: Gunmen set fire to a room in Gidan Taba village in Maradun, killing 12 members of one family including women and children, and abducted more residents. Name the dead where the source does; the structural why is a north-west where banditry has outlasted every federal security campaign — and it lands as 30 state assemblies have just approved state police.

stories.label: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's letter to staff about affair
stories.summary: Nvidia's board has opened an independent investigation and Huang stays on as CEO, after his letter to staff about an affair (TMTPost: Asian chip shares rebounded while Nvidia's off-hours trading kept falling). Lead with the governance mechanism — what an independent review can do to the founder of the world's most valuable chip company — not the personal detail. Only link it to this week's falls in SK Hynix, Broadcom and ASML if a source does.

stories.label: 227亿，史上最大AI界发电机大单来了！
stories.summary: Anthropic paid $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy generators from OnePWR, taking over a Caterpillar order placed two years ago before prices soared — the largest known power-equipment purchase by an AI lab (via the FT). Lead with the number and the mechanism: turbine and generator lead times now run years, so labs are buying their own power plants and bypassing utilities, as xAI and Alphabet did. Note the ~$900bn compute commitment to 2045 and Blackstone's warning of a junk credit rating ahead of the IPO.

stories.label: ByteDance reportedly weighs expanding its Brazil data center project
stories.summary: ByteDance is seeking developers for a second phase at the Port of Pecém in Ceará, larger than the 300-megawatt project already under construction. Lead with where it lands: Brazil's semi-arid north-east, and the water, power and data-sovereignty questions a Chinese platform's compute hub raises there. Dateline Pecém, Brazil.

stories.label: BTC news: Binance's bitcoin mining pool finds just one block in a week as shutdown nears
stories.summary: Binance's mining pool, which once handled a large share of the network, found one block in a week as it shuts down, and its miners are moving their hashrate to rival pools. Lead with where that power goes: the shutdown concentrates block production in fewer large pools, which is the network's real centralisation risk. Series: bitcoin.

stories.label: Despite sacrificing people after catastrophic El Niño flooding, ancient societies were generally peaceful
stories.summary: A survey of the Lambayeque Valley in northern Peru finds violence was extremely rare even through El Niño floods, overturning the assumption that the mass sacrifices on that coast were part of scarcity-driven warfare. Lead with the surprise — ritual killing without a collapse into war — and what it says about how societies absorb climate shocks.

stories.label: Pope Leo leaves Uruguay and heads to fraught tour stop in Milei's Argentina
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina, the visit Francis never made, into an open clash between the Catholic Church and Javier Milei's austerity programme. Lead with what the Church has said about the cuts and who bears them — pensioners, soup kitchens, the poor the Church feeds — not the itinerary; the structural story is a moral institution with mass reach confronting a libertarian government on its own ground.

stories.label: Trump says fresh strikes on Iran 'highly unlikely' if talks progress
stories.summary: The war is shifting into a negotiating channel: an Iraqi delegation spent eight hours in Tehran handing over a US message, Trump says new strikes are 'highly unlikely' if Iran signs 'a very strong agreement' on its nuclear programme and reopens the Strait of Hormuz, and Araghchi answers that Washington must choose between a deal and a war it would lose. Lead with the Iraqi mediation and the terms Trump attached; the Israel-Iran ceasefire market went from 65% to 92% this week. Attribute the Iraqi-message report to Al Arabiya sources via TASS, and Araghchi's remarks to Mehr. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: Eisenkot says Israel in 'devastating diplomatic crisis' as he seeks to form govt
stories.summary: New since Eisenkot received the mandate: he has begun reaching out to Netanyahu's own allies, and the Arab Joint List, with 19 seats, says it will back him from outside to keep Netanyahu from returning but will not join a cabinet. Lead with the arithmetic: the first post-Netanyahu government may depend on Palestinian citizens' parties it will not seat. Attribute the Joint List position to Jabareen via TASS. Datelined Jerusalem.

stories.label: Auto policy sets $6bn export target over five years
stories.summary: Pakistan's new auto policy, approved only after the IMF signed off, puts a development levy on conventional cars to pay for EV and export incentives, exempts cars up to 1,000cc, and caps the advance a manufacturer may demand at 20% of the price. Lead with the IMF's veto over industrial policy and the $6bn export target, against an industry that has mostly assembled for a protected home market. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: Will US inflation data ease affordability concerns?
stories.summary: After Friday's jobs report, traders price about a 78% chance that Kevin Warsh's Fed raises rates on 9 December, with the S&P 500 5.6% below its October high; Tuesday's October CPI is expected to keep that pressure on, days after Democrats won Congress campaigning on affordability. Lead with a Fed set to hike into a falling market, and who pays: borrowers and the dollar-debt countries outside the US. Name the Fed funds rate and US inflation for the charts. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Iran's oil storage facilities 80% restored -- NIOEC CEO
stories.summary: Iran's state refiner says 80% of its bombed oil storage is back and fuel-pumping facilities are 60% rebuilt, and that Tehran's fuel supply came back within two weeks of the strikes on the Rey depot. Lead with what the war did to the domestic fuel system and how quickly it was patched while the blockade holds. This is the NIOEC chief speaking to Russian state agency TASS: attribute every figure and do not state them as fact. Name Brent crude. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: Stablecoin market cap is frozen. The money inside it isn't
stories.summary: Stablecoin supply has barely grown this year, but the money in it moves faster, and payments are only about 0.5% of the value transferred on-chain; the rest is trading and internal shuffling. Lead with that 0.5%: it punctures the headline 'transfer volume' figures used to sell stablecoins as a payments rail to regulators and remittance users. Name bitcoin for the chart only if the piece ties to it. Datelined New York.

stories.label: What the election results mean for crypto: State of Crypto
stories.summary: With Democrats taking both chambers by large margins, the crypto industry that spent heavily on the midterms faces a Congress that can subpoena it and is unlikely to pass the market-structure bill it wanted. Lead with what changes in January: which bills die, and which oversight powers return. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: 'South Africans entering Nigeria to help cartels traffic drugs,' security briefing told
stories.summary: A Nigerian anti-drug official turns around the familiar South African claim that Nigerians run the drug trade: South Africans are now being arrested in Nigeria working for cartels on a route that runs through Mozambique to Mexican networks. Lead with the arrests and the route, the mechanism by which Latin American cartels use African couriers and ports. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: Liquid-assisted crystal growth cuts perovskite defects for efficient solar cells and LEDs
stories.summary: A Korean-American team (Sungkyunkwan, KRICT, UC San Diego, Princeton) grew perovskite films through a liquid phase that sharply cuts the crystal defects which make perovskite solar cells degrade, and made both efficient solar cells and LEDs from the same film. Lead with the defect reduction and the efficiency figure, and say what it does and does not fix about perovskites' durability problem. Datelined Suwon.

stories.label: Egypt train collision kills 4, injures 88 in Giza
stories.summary: Update to this morning's El Ayyat derailment, which we reported from TASS with injuries only: the Health Ministry now counts at least seven dead and more than 112 injured on the Cairo-Aswan line. Lead with the death toll, then the mechanism: Egypt's state railway has had repeated fatal crashes despite a multibillion-dollar modernisation programme, and the passengers on the southern Upper Egypt line are among the country's poorest. Use the independent sources (Al Jazeera, BBC, The New Arab) so the earlier state-media-only report is superseded.

stories.label: Turkiye, Azerbaijan leaders vow unity after tensions
stories.summary: Erdogan and Aliyev used the sixth anniversary of Karabakh's recapture, in Shusha, to paper over a public rift that opened in September when Baku revised its school uniform rules. Lead with the rift itself — a dispute over religious dress inside the region's closest Muslim alliance — then why both need each other: the Middle Corridor, gas pipelines to Europe, and Türkiye's role in the South Caucasus peace with Armenia.

stories.label: Russia strikes power substations in Ukraine and three ships in Black Sea
stories.summary: The new development since this morning's grid story: Russia says it hit three cargo vessels in the Black Sea it claims carried military goods for Ukraine, on top of substations that left 600,000+ in Dnipropetrovsk without power. Lead with the ships — strikes on merchant shipping to Odesa threaten Ukraine's grain-export corridor and push up war-risk insurance — and attribute the 'military goods' claim to Russia's defence ministry.

stories.label: Rags and riches -- how SA retail giants profit off sweatshops
stories.summary: Court documents and government raids show South African clothing factories supplying the big local retailers pay below minimum wage in 'deplorable' conditions — 'buy local' is no guarantee against exploitation. Lead with the documented case (a worker who gave birth to twins on a Newcastle factory floor) and the mechanism: retailers' buying terms push suppliers into non-compliance while the brands keep their distance. Name the retailers the investigation names.

stories.label: 100 buses long: Scientists map one of the world's largest known coral colonies
stories.summary: Researchers mapped a single coral colony stretching more than 1.5 km along the outer reef of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands in the Indian Ocean, one of the largest ever recorded. Lead with the scale, then what it teaches: a colony that size has survived centuries of heatwaves, which makes it a natural record of reef resilience as bleaching spreads.

stories.label: NASA Unveils Moon Base Awards at MAX POWER
stories.summary: NASA handed out a batch of Moon Base contracts — new lunar lander awards and a recycled Mars rover — days after China's Long March 10 docking test in lunar orbit. Lead with who won what and for how much, and the structural point: the US lunar base is being built by private contractors on fixed-price awards, a race with China's state programme for the south pole.

stories.label: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
stories.summary: Iran hanged Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh, accused by state media of Molotov and grenade attacks during January's anti-government protests. Lead with the names and the charge, then the mechanism: wartime security courts turning protest cases into capital cases while the country is under US blockade. Name who carried out the sentences, say what rights groups report about the trials, and count where this puts executions linked to the January protests.

stories.label: Strait of Hormuz fully under IRGC Navy control: spox
stories.summary: The new development since our last Hormuz story: a third tanker is now ablaze, UKMTO separately confirms a tanker fire 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman with the crew evacuated, and the IRGC claims full control of the strait, warning that ships off its sanctioned route risk mines. Attribute IRGC claims as Iranian state media; UKMTO and Middle East Eye are the independent check. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude: what it means for the crews, the insurers and the oil importers in Asia who depend on the route.

stories.label: 'Allegations of Jensen Huang's involvement with a Chinese spy' impact?···Madison Huang abruptly cancels Korea visit ahead of Nvidia AI Day
stories.summary: US officials believe Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive said to be close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, is a Chinese intelligence asset, and Madison Huang has cancelled her Seoul visit ahead of Nvidia's AI Day with Samsung and Hyundai. The mechanism is export control: Megaspeed's place in the chip trade and what the allegation means for Washington's scrutiny of how Nvidia hardware reaches China. Keep the allegation attributed: nobody has been charged. Mention that Broadcom and SK Hynix shares also fell this week, but don't claim this story caused it.

stories.label: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave hundreds of thousands without electricity
stories.summary: About 850,000 people lost power, more than 600,000 of them in Dnipropetrovsk, after an overnight Russian attack on energy facilities, on the day the Zaporizhzhia plant lost its last external line. Lead with the civilians left without heat as winter starts, then the mechanism: a deliberate campaign against the grid running while Russia sends a higher-level delegation to the Abu Dhabi talks.

stories.label: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
stories.summary: Physicists measured shot noise in cuprates to test whether electrons pair up in the 'pseudogap' state above the temperature where superconductivity starts, a question open since the late 1980s. Lead with the method, since noise tells you the size of the charge carriers, then why it matters: knowing whether pairs form before superconductivity does is a step towards superconductors that work without extreme cooling.

stories.label: These Finland homes get free heat from bitcoin miners (as long as BTC stays above $70,000)
stories.summary: In Nokia, Finland, a 180-square-metre house now heats itself with the waste heat from bitcoin mining rigs, so the household's heating bill is paid by the bitcoin price. Lead with the break-even: the scheme pays only while bitcoin stays above $70,000, and SunBit's payback maths leaves out the 2028 halving, which cuts mining rewards in half. The mechanism to teach is a household turning an energy cost into a commodity bet.

stories.label: 华为、OpenAI、字节等科技巨头为何都要插手制药？
stories.summary: Huawei, OpenAI and ByteDance are all moving into drug discovery. Tell it from the Chinese industry side: what each company is building, which drug makers they have signed with, and where AI actually shortens the pipeline (target finding, molecule screening) and where it does not (clinical trials). Lead with the most concrete deal or result in the piece rather than the hype.

stories.label: 2027 Politics Watch: From Asaba rally's death to Obi's subsidy challenge
stories.summary: One person was killed and five injured at an opposition procession in Asaba, and police say they had been warned beforehand. Lead with the death and the question of why a warned police force did not prevent it, then set it against the wider 2027 campaign: Obi's challenge on the fuel subsidy and the Tinubu–Atiku fight over university funding. The pattern to show is political violence starting more than a year before the vote.

stories.label: At least 150 injured in train crash in northern Egypt -- media
stories.summary: Four carriages derailed at El-Ayyat in Giza governorate, injuring at least 150 people, and more than 50 ambulances were sent, according to Masrawy as relayed by TASS (attribute it). El-Ayyat has had deadly derailments before. The accountability angle is Egypt's rail-safety record and its modernisation spending, and what the authorities say caused this crash.

stories.label: Cops verify terror claim after Ghaziabad police outpost blast
stories.summary: A blast hit the Vasundhara police outpost in Ghaziabad, on Delhi's edge, and a militant group has claimed it. Uttar Pradesh's Anti-Terrorism Squad is checking the claim and possible links to a wider network. Report what is established and what is only claimed. Do not name a group as responsible beyond its own claim, and watch for any collective suspicion falling on local Muslims.

stories.label: Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh damaged by falling debris after attempted attack, ministry says
stories.summary: New development on the Houthi-Saudi exchange: Saudi Arabia's own Energy Ministry now confirms an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh was damaged by debris after Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted over the capital, and a Reuters witness saw windows blown out across several floors — the first independent confirmation after days of Houthi-only claims. Lead with the hit in the capital, not a remote oil field; tie it to Saudi strikes on Yemen (1,039 killed or wounded since July 13, per Yemen's health ministry) and to Brent crude, as the war now reaches the headquarters city of the world's largest oil exporter.

stories.label: Earthquake hits central Japan, injuring more than 20 people
stories.summary: A strong quake centred on Aichi shattered windows and injured at least 22 people across central Japan's industrial belt; Shinkansen trains ran at reduced speed as a precaution. Lead with the injuries and where the shaking hit, then the mechanism: how Japan's early-warning and rail-safety systems kept a quake in its most densely built manufacturing corridor from turning deadly. File as a disaster, not science.

stories.label: External power line to ZNPP disconnected due to damage
stories.summary: Europe's largest nuclear plant, Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia, lost its external power line (Ferrosplavnaya-1) and is running on backup diesel generators to keep reactor cooling going. Both sides report it (TASS and Ukrainska Pravda) — attribute who blames whom. Lead with the diesel fallback and how many times the plant has been cut off; the mechanism is that cooling of spent fuel depends on one line amid strikes on the grid while Abu Dhabi talks continue.

stories.label: Armed Maoists eliminated, but 'dimagi Naxals' remain a threat: PM Modi
stories.summary: Speaking at a CRPF CoBRA base in Bastar, Modi declared India's armed Maoist insurgency over, then named a new target: 'dimagi Naxals' ("brain Naxals") he says have infiltrated parties and organisations. Lead with the pivot — the end of a decades-long war in India's adivasi forest belt is being used to recast ideological opponents and civil society as security threats. Who bears the cost: the Bastar adivasis displaced by the campaign and activists who could now be labelled.

stories.label: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
stories.summary: Donations to India's main opposition party, Congress, fell nearly 75% — the sharpest drop in a decade — per its filings with the Election Commission. Lead with the number and the gap against the BJP's haul; the mechanism is where corporate political money flows after the Supreme Court struck down electoral bonds, and what an opposition starved of funds means for Indian democracy. Use the Economic Times article; the mint URL in the cluster is a mismatched Kalpataru story.

stories.label: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of efforts against terrorism
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans 'faceless' anti-terrorism courts — judges and prosecutors kept anonymous — and Rs70bn for counter-terrorism police in a year. Lead with the faceless courts: a model tried in Peru and Colombia that protects judges from militant reprisal but strips defendants of a known accuser and open trial. Context: Pakistan says attacks are launched from Afghan soil, and Pak-Afghan trade stays frozen over it (Dawn, same day).

stories.label: Why raising prices in Japan amid 'insanely high' inflation backfires on firms
stories.summary: Uniqlo reversed a sock price rise within days and Saizeriya apologised for raising its doria price: Japanese firms facing record input costs from a weak yen cannot pass them on to consumers raised in three decades of deflation. Lead with the Uniqlo U-turn; the mechanism is how an entrenched deflationary mindset squeezes margins and complicates the Bank of Japan's exit from easy money. Name the yen.

stories.label: Europe withdraws 5% of gas injected into UGS facilities in summer in just ten days
stories.summary: An early-November cold snap has Europe drawing gas from underground storage at a record pace — 5% of everything injected over the summer gone in ten days — from reserves that started the winter at historically low levels. Russian state agency TASS computed this from Gas Infrastructure Europe data: attribute it, and lead with the drawdown rate and what it means for natural gas prices and household bills if the cold holds, with Hormuz LNG flows disrupted.

stories.label: Antipersonnel mines have returned in Ukraine and now threaten the world | New Scientist
stories.summary: 3D printers, cheap microcontrollers and drone delivery have revived the antipersonnel mine nearly three decades after the 1997 Ottawa Treaty — Ukraine's war has made them cheaper, deadlier and easy to build. Lead with the technology that undid the ban; the stakes are civilians, who are most landmine victims, and the export of these designs to every conflict after Ukraine.

stories.label: 从资本密集到人力密集：全球AI的瓶颈，卡在缺乏“电工”
stories.summary: The AI build-out's bottleneck has moved from GPUs to power to electrical equipment, and now to electricians: capital can buy equipment delivery slots but cannot shorten the years it takes to train a skilled tradesperson. A Chinese tech-press view — lead with the claim that compute expansion is now limited by labour, not money, and what that means for the US-China data-centre race.

stories.label: 登月的胜负手，不在火箭点火那一刻
stories.summary: China's crewed Moon plan uses two Long March 10 launches with docking in lunar orbit, aimed at a lasting Earth-Moon transport system with a distant retrograde orbit (DRO) hub and deep-space tracking, rather than a one-off landing. Contrast it with Artemis's dependence on commercial contractors and its delays. The inside view: what China is building beyond the rocket launch.

stories.label: How Earth Lost a Billion Years of Its History
stories.summary: Earth's rock record is missing up to a billion years before the Cambrian, 538 million years ago — the 'Great Unconformity'. A new study says the rise and break-up of ancient supercontinents eroded it away. Lead with the size of the gap; the mechanism links plate tectonics to why we can't read the run-up to complex life, and possibly to the chemistry that triggered it.

stories.label: Iran, Russia stressed deepening security, defense cooperation
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, met Vladimir Putin, and Iran's ambassador says they agreed to deepen security and defence ties and the North–South Transport Corridor. Attribute to Iranian state agency Mehr. Lead with the timing: on the day the US moved to blockade Iran's land and Caspian routes, Tehran's security chief is in Moscow discussing exactly those routes.

stories.label: New Zealand preliminary vote leaves unclear who will govern
stories.summary: Preliminary results give Christopher Luxon's National-led coalition a slim majority with about 14% of votes (special votes) still uncounted, so New Zealand waits weeks for a government. Lead with the margin and the uncounted share; explain how special votes have shifted seats in past MMP elections and which partner (ACT, NZ First) holds the leverage. Fills the Oceania gap flagged by the daily audit.

stories.label: Two tankers explode, burn in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: New since the 11-06 and 11-07 coverage: the IRGC Navy says two more tankers on an 'unauthorized route' struck mines overnight and are burning, UKMTO logged a fresh incident with a bulk carrier 18nm off Khorfakkan, explosions were heard again on Qeshm, and Iran's army says Hormuz stays closed. The claim of mines and 'violating' ships is the IRGC's, via Iranian and Russian state media — attribute it. Lead with Iran running a permit regime by mine: ships either take Tehran's route or risk the minefield. Chart ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Pakistan's Hormuz agreement with Iran faces test after LNG tanker attack
stories.summary: Pakistan negotiated its own safe-passage understanding with Tehran, yet a Pakistan-bound LNG carrier (Qatari gas) was attacked. The mechanism: Pakistan imports most of its LNG from Qatar through Hormuz, so a bilateral deal with Iran was its only hedge, and it just failed. Lead with what the country's power and fertilizer plants depend on, and the push to diversify gas suppliers. Chart natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Canary Islands' El Hierro declares emergency amid migrant, refugee influx
stories.summary: More than 3,300 people reached El Hierro — an island of about 11,000 — by boat in the first week of November, and its authorities declared an emergency and asked Madrid for help. Lead with the ratio. The structural why: the Atlantic route from Senegal, Mauritania and Mali is the deadliest into Europe, and it swells when Mediterranean routes close. Name who is fleeing and from what, not just the arrivals count.

stories.label: Bomb-laden drone attack on a military base in Colombia! 5 soldiers killed
stories.summary: Explosive-laden drones hit a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar, killing 5 soldiers and wounding 33 (8 seriously). Lead with the toll and the weapon: Colombia's armed groups (ELN and Gulf Clan factions contest southern Bolívar's gold-mining zone) now use the cheap drone warfare seen in Ukraine and Sudan. Name the suspected group only if the authorities do.

stories.label: Saudi raids leave 1,039 dead, wounded in Yemen
stories.summary: New figure since the 11-07 Sanaa-strike story: Yemen's (Sanaa-based) health minister puts the toll of Saudi strikes since July 13 at 1,039 killed or wounded, with bodies still being pulled from homes in Bani Hushaysh, Sanaa province. Attribute the count to the Houthi-run ministry via Iranian state media. Lead with the cumulative toll on civilians — the escalation of the Saudi-Houthi front is the story the daily audit is watching.

stories.label: Govt urged to pursue review of FCC verdict on workplace harassment laws
stories.summary: Pakistan's new Federal Constitutional Court read workplace-harassment law narrowly, and a National Assembly committee now presses the government to pursue its review petition. Lead with what the ruling removes — which conduct and which workers fall outside protection — and the precedent: the FCC, created by the 27th Amendment, is reshaping rights law within its first year.

stories.label: 'Special master' named for ethics probe in lawsuit over Trump's DC golf project
stories.summary: A federal judge will appoint a former top federal prosecutor to investigate whether Justice Department lawyers committed ethical violations defending Trump's plan to close and renovate a historic public golf course in Washington (Reuters). Lead with the rare step: a court probing the government's own lawyers' conduct. The accountability mechanism is the story, not the golf.

stories.label: 中国白酒出口韩国暴涨85%，谁在买？
stories.summary: Chinese baijiu exports to South Korea jumped 85%, while the liquor sells weakly at home. Lead with the number and who is buying — Korean drinkers mixing it, Chinese diaspora, tourism — and the mechanism: distillers facing a domestic slump turning to export markets, as China's wider consumer weakness pushes producers abroad.

stories.label: Why the tropics lose the most birds when cities expand
stories.summary: A new study finds urban expansion strips the most bird diversity in the tropics, where species are most numerous and most specialized. Lead with the size of the loss and the mechanism (narrow niches, little tolerance for cities), and the stakes: most of the world's urban growth to 2050 is in tropical Africa and Asia. Name the journal.
